One day, Tom and Lily ask their mom if they can watch the screen. Mom says, "No, not now. You have watched the screen a lot today. It is time to do something else. The screen is not always useful. It can make your eyes and brain tired. You need to use your imagination and creativity."

Tom and Lily are sad. They want to watch the screen. They think the screen is fun and useful. They say, "Please, mom, please. Just a little bit more. We like the screen. It makes us happy and smart."

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, I do not permit you to watch the screen now. You have to listen to me. I know what is good for you. You can watch the screen later, after you play outside and have dinner. Now, go and find something else to do. You have many toys and books. You can also draw or sing or dance."

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite one was Rosie. Rosie had a pink dress, brown hair and blue eyes. Lily liked to pretend that Rosie was her best friend.

One day, Lily decided to invite Rosie to have a tea party. She set up a small table and two chairs in her room. She brought some cups, plates and cookies from the kitchen. She poured some water into the cups and pretended it was tea. She gave one cup and one plate to Rosie and said, "Here you go, Rosie. This is for you. You are my guest."

Rosie did not say anything, because she was a doll. But Lily did not mind. She talked to Rosie as if she could hear her. She asked her about her day, her hobbies and her dreams. She told her about her own things, too. She said, "I like to draw, to read and to dance. Do you like those things, too, Rosie? I hope you do. We have so much in common."

Lily was a little dog who loved to play with her friends. She liked to run, jump, and bark with them in the park. But there was one thing that made her very scared: thunder. Whenever she heard a loud boom in the sky, she would tremble and hide under the bed.

One day, she was playing with her friends when a big storm came. The sky became dark and the wind blew hard. Lily heard a boom and ran to her home. She did not say goodbye to her friends. She just wanted to be safe under the bed.

But when she got to her home, she saw that the door was closed. Her family was not there. They had gone to the shop and forgot to leave the door open for her. Lily felt sad and alone. Suddenly, help arrived! Two boats came up from shore. They picked up Mia and Mark from their kayak and took them back to land. Mia and Mark were so happy and relieved. They learned their lesson and never went kayaking so deep in the lake again.

"Let's make a loop here," Lily says, pointing to a spot on the floor.

"No, let's make a loop there," Ben says, pointing to another spot.

They both insist on their own loop. They start to argue and pull the track pieces.

"Stop it, you are breaking the track!" Lily shouts.

"Stop it, you are making it wrong!" Ben shouts.

They are not having fun anymore. They are making each other sad and angry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken track and the unhappy children.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks.

"Lily and Ben are fighting over the loop," Mom says.

"Why are you fighting over the loop?" Mom asks.

"Because I want it here and he wants it there," Lily says.

"Because I want it there and she wants it here," Ben says.

Mom thinks for a moment. She has an idea.

"Why don't you make two loops, one for each of you?" Mom suggests.

"Two loops?" Lily and Ben repeat.

"Yes, two loops. You can make them next to each other or far apart. You can make them big or small. You can make them any way you like. As long as you share the track pieces and play nicely," Mom says.

Lily and Ben look at each other. They think Mom's idea is smart. They nod and smile.

"Okay, let's make two loops," Lily says.

"Okay, let's make two loops," Ben says.

They start to fix the track and make their own loops. They stop arguing and start talking.

"Look, my loop is big and round," Lily says.

"Look, my loop is small and twisty," Ben says.

They admire each other's loops. They are proud of their work. They are having fun again.

"Choo choo, here comes the red train," Lily says.

"Choo choo, here comes the blue train," Ben says.

They are happy and friendly. They thank Mom for her smart idea.

"Thank you, Mom, for the two loops," Lily says.

"Thank you, Mom, for the two loops," Ben says.

Mom smiles and hugs them.

"You're welcome, my sweeties. I'm glad you are playing well together. You are both very smart and creative," Mom says.

They shrank some more cars, some flowers, some bugs and some rocks. They made a tiny maze with the rocks and put the cars and the bugs inside. They watched them race and crawl.

"Look, my car is faster than your bug," Tom said.

"No, it's not. My bug is smarter than your car," Lily said.

They laughed and cheered for their toys.

But then, something bad happened. The bottle tipped over and spilled some juice on Tom and Lily. They shrank to the size of peas too.

"Help! We are small!" Tom shouted.

"Help! We are in the maze!" Lily shouted.

They tried to find a way out, but the rocks were too big and the bugs were too scary. They were lost and scared.

"Tom, I don't like this. I want to be big again," Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. Me too," Tom said.

They hugged each other and hoped that someone would find them and make them big again.

They heard a loud noise. It was their mom. She came to the garden and saw the bottle and the maze.

"What is this mess?" she asked.

She picked up the bottle and read the label.

"Shrink Juice? Oh no. Where are Tom and Lily?" she asked.

She looked around and saw two tiny voices coming from the maze.

"Mom! Mom! We are here! We are small!" Tom and Lily cried.

She saw them and gasped.

"Oh, my babies! What have you done?" she asked.

She quickly poured some water on them and they grew back to their normal size.

"Mom! You saved us!" Tom and Lily said.

They ran to her and hugged her.

"I'm so glad you are okay. But you should never play with things you don't know. They can be dangerous," she said.

"I'm sorry, mom. We were curious. We won't do it again," Tom and Lily said.

They apologized and helped her clean up the mess. They threw away the bottle and the shrank toys. They decided to play with their normal cars and their normal bugs instead. They learned their lesson and never touched the shrink juice again.

Mia and Leo were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things in the water, like fish, crabs and shells. They also saw a big boat with people on it.

"Look, mom, a boat!" Mia said, pointing to the boat.

"Yes, dear, that's a boat. They are going fishing," mom said.

"Can we go fishing too?" Leo asked.

"Maybe another day, honey. We don't have a boat or a fishing rod," dad said.

Mia and Leo nodded. They went back to their sandcastle. They used a bucket and a shovel to make it. They decorated it with shells and seaweed. They were very proud of their sandcastle. It was beautiful.

Suddenly, they heard a loud scream from the boat. They looked up and saw a big shark jumping out of the water. It had sharp teeth and a fin. It tried to bite the boat and the people.

"Wow, a shark!" Leo said, scared and excited.

"Shh, Leo, don't shout. The shark might hear us," Mia said, squeezing his hand.

"Are they okay, mom?" Mia asked, looking at mom.

"I hope so, dear. The shark is very dangerous. It can hurt the people and the boat," mom said, holding them close.

"Can we help them, dad?" Leo asked, looking at dad.

"I don't think so, son. The shark is too big and too fast. We have to stay here and be safe," dad said, watching the boat.

They saw the people on the boat throwing things at the shark. They heard a loud bang. They saw the shark swim away. They saw the boat turn around and come back to the shore.

"Yay, they made it!" Mia said, clapping her hands.

"They are very brave!" Leo said, cheering.

They saw the people get off the boat. They had cuts and bruises, but they were smiling. They thanked the people who helped them. They saw Mia and Leo and their mom and dad. They waved at them.

"Hi, kids, you have a beautiful sandcastle!" one of them said.

"Thank you!" Mia and Leo said, smiling.

They were happy that the people were safe. They were happy that the shark was gone. They were happy that they had a beautiful sandcastle. They hugged their mom and dad. They had a fun day at the beach.

But then they heard a loud meow. They looked around and saw a cat. The cat was black and white and had green eyes. The cat was gazing at their bricks. The cat looked hungry and curious.

Lily and Tom were not happy. They did not want the cat to ruin their bricks. They said no and shooed. The cat did not listen. The cat kept playing with their bricks. The cat made a mess of their work.

Lily and Tom were sad and angry. They decided to make a plan. They got some cheese and bread from the kitchen. They put them in a basket. They took the basket to the yard. They showed the cat the cheese and bread. The cat stopped gazing at their bricks. The cat gazed at the cheese and bread. The cat was very hungry and wanted to eat.

Lily liked to paint. She had many colors and brushes. She painted flowers and trees and animals. She was happy when she painted.

Tom was Lily's brother. He was lazy. He did not like to paint. He liked to watch TV and play games. He was bored when Lily painted.

One day, Lily was painting a big picture on the wall. She wanted to show it to Mom and Dad. She used red and blue and yellow and green. She made a rainbow and a sun and a bird.

Tom saw Lily painting. He was angry. He wanted to watch TV, but Lily was too loud. He said, "Stop painting, Lily! You are making a mess! I want to watch TV!"

Lily said, "No, Tom! I like painting! It is fun! You can watch TV later. Let me finish my picture!"

Tom did not listen. He grabbed Lily's brush and threw it away. He took her paint and spilled it on the floor. He tore her picture from the wall. He said, "There! Now you can't paint anymore!"

Lily was sad. She cried. She felt pain in her heart. She said, "Tom, you are mean! You ruined my picture! You made me sad! Why did you do that?"

Tom did not care. He laughed. He said, "Because I can! You are silly! Painting is stupid! TV is better!"

Mom and Dad came home. They saw the mess. They saw Lily crying. They saw Tom laughing. They were angry. They said, "Tom, what did you do? You are in big trouble! You hurt Lily and you wasted the paint! You have to clean up and say sorry! You can't watch TV for a week!"

Tom was shocked. He did not like that. He said, "No, Mom and Dad! That is not fair! Lily started it! She was painting on the wall! She was annoying me!"

Mom and Dad did not believe him. They said, "Tom, you are lying! Lily was painting nicely. You were lazy and rude. You have to learn to be nice and share. You have to respect Lily and her painting. You have to say sorry and hug her!"

Tom did not want to do that. He said, "No, Mom and Dad! I don't want to say sorry! I don't want to hug her! I don't like her! I don't like painting!"

Mom and Dad were sad. They said, "Tom, you are making us sad. You are making Lily sad. You are making yourself sad. You have to change your attitude. You have to be a good brother. You have to try painting. You might like it. It might make you happy."

Tom did not listen. He said, "No, Mom and Dad! I don't want to change! I don't want to be a good brother! I don't want to try painting! I don't want to be happy! I want to watch TV!"

Mom and Dad shook their heads. They said, "Tom, you are being stubborn. You are being selfish. You are being foolish. You are missing out on a lot of fun and love. You are making a bad choice. You are making a bad ending."

Tom did not care. He said, "No, Mom and Dad! I don't care! I don't care! I don't care!"

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that friends should share and help each other, not be selfish and mean. It also shows that saying sorry and forgiving are important when someone makes a mistake.

"Can we help it?" Lily asked Tom.

"No, we can't," Tom said. "When something is dead, it can't come back to life. We can only say goodbye and bury it."

Lily and Tom dug a hole in the ground. They put the bird in the hole and covered it with dirt. They found some stones and made a cross. They said a prayer for the bird.

"Goodbye, bird," Lily said. "We are sorry you are dead. We hope you are happy in heaven."

"Goodbye, bird," Tom said. "We will remember you. You were a beautiful bird."

They hugged each other and went back to play. They saw the butterfly again. It was flying near the calendar. It landed on the picture of spring.

"Look, Tom," Lily said. "The butterfly is saying hello to the bird. It is telling it that spring is here and that life goes on."

Tom smiled. He agreed with Lily. He felt a little better.

"Yes, Lily," Tom said. "Spring is here and life goes on. And we are here to enjoy it."

Tom was a restless boy who liked to question everything. He always asked his mom and dad why the sky was blue, why the grass was green, why the sun was hot, and so on. Sometimes they had answers, sometimes they did not.

One day, Tom found a big book in his dad's study. It had many strange words and pictures on it. Tom was curious and opened the book. He saw a word that looked like this: A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A. He wondered what it meant.

He ran to his mom and showed her the book. "Mom, what is this word?" he asked.

Mom looked at the book and smiled. "That is a spell, Tom. It is a word that some people use to do magic. But you have to be careful with spells. They can be good or bad."

Tom was amazed. He wanted to do magic. He asked his mom, "Can I say the spell, Mom? Can I do magic?"

Mom shook her head. "No, Tom. You are too young to say spells. You don't know what they can do. Maybe they can make things disappear, or change, or fly. Maybe they can make you happy, or sad, or scared. You have to be very careful with spells. They are not for playing."

Tom was disappointed. He wanted to try the spell. He thought his mom was just being mean. He decided to wait until his mom was busy and then say the spell. He thought it would be fun.

He hid the book under his bed and waited for his mom to go to the kitchen. When she did, he took the book and ran to the backyard. He looked around and saw a big tree. He thought it would be cool to make the tree fly. He opened the book and found the spell. He said it out loud: "A-B-R-A-C-A-D-A-B-R-A!"

Suddenly, the tree shook and lifted off the ground. Tom was shocked and happy. He had done magic! He laughed and clapped his hands. He said the spell again and again, making the tree go higher and higher.

But then, something went wrong. The tree stopped flying and started falling. It was falling fast and hard. It was falling towards Tom. Tom was scared and sorry. He had done a bad spell. He wanted to stop it. He tried to say the spell backwards, but he could not remember it. He screamed for his mom.

Mom heard Tom's scream and ran to the backyard. She saw the tree falling and Tom in danger. She was scared and angry. She grabbed Tom and pulled him away from the tree. The tree crashed to the ground, making a loud noise and a big mess.

Mom hugged Tom and checked if he was hurt. He was not, but he was crying. He was sorry for what he had done. He told his mom he had said the spell and made the tree fly and fall. He said he was sorry and he would never say spells again.

Mom was relieved and glad that Tom was safe. She was also sad and mad that Tom had disobeyed her and used the book. She told Tom he had been very naughty and foolish. She told him he had to go to his room and think about what he had done. She told him he had to give back the book and never touch it again.

Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He gave back the book and went to his room. He felt bad and scared. He wished he had listened to his mom. He learned that spells were not for playing. He learned that questioning everything was not always good. He learned that being restless could get him in trouble. He decided to be a good boy from now on. He decided to be more careful with words. He decided to be more happy with what he had. He decided to be more thankful for his mom. He decided to say a different word: "I love you, Mom."

Tom saw Sara sucking her thumb and said, "Sara, stop sucking your thumb! You are too big for that. You will have bad teeth and people will laugh at you."

Sara felt hurt and angry. She said, "No, I won't stop. I like my thumb. It is my friend. You are mean and you don't understand me." She ran away from Tom and hid behind a tree. She sucked her thumb harder and cried.

Mom saw Sara and Tom fighting and went to talk to them. She hugged Sara and said, "Sara, I know you love your thumb, but Tom is right. Sucking your thumb too much is not good for you. You have other ways to cope with your feelings. You can hug a toy, read a book, sing a song, or talk to me or Tom. We love you and we want you to be happy and healthy."

Sara listened to Mom and felt a little better. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I didn't know sucking my thumb was bad. I just wanted to feel comfortable. But I don't want to have bad teeth or be lonely. I want to be happy and healthy. Can you help me stop sucking my thumb?"

Sara liked the idea. She said, "Yes, Mom. That sounds fun. Thank you for helping me. And thank you, Tom, for telling me the truth. I'm sorry I was mean to you. Can we play together?"

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a bee. It was angry and flew towards them. It wanted the club. It was its home.

"Help, help!" Lily cried. "The bee is coming!"

"Maybe this will do something," he said.

"Uh-oh," Ben said. "What did we do?"

The bee saw them. It was happy. It flew down and picked up the club. It took it back to its nest.

"Hello," they said. "We are Lily and Ben. We are children. We shrank by accident. Can you help us?"

The ladybug smiled. It was friendly.

"Maybe I can," it said. "I know a lot of things in the garden. Maybe I can find something to make you grow back. Come with me. I'll show you around."

Lily and Ben felt hopeful. They climbed on the ladybug's back. It flew away with them.

They saw many wonderful things. They saw a spider web, a butterfly, a mushroom, a pond. They saw other bugs and animals. They learned their names and stories.

They had fun. They forgot they were tiny. They made new friends.

They also found something to make them grow back. It was a magic berry. It was blue and shiny and had a sweet smell.

The ladybug gave it to them.

"Eat this," it said. "It will make you big again. But be careful. Only eat a little bit. Too much will make you too big."

Lily and Ben thanked the ladybug. They each took a bite of the berry. They felt a tingling in their bodies. They started to grow.

They grew back to their normal size. They were happy. They hugged the ladybug.

"Thank you, thank you!" they said. "You are the best!"

The ladybug was happy too. It hugged them back.

"You are welcome, welcome!" it said. "You are the best too!"

They said goodbye to the ladybug and the other creatures. They promised to visit them again.

They ran back to their house. They told their parents what happened. Their parents did not believe them. They thought they made up the story.

But Lily and Ben knew it was true. They had a secret. They kept the club. It was still small. They hid it in their pocket.

They smiled at each other. They had a big adventure. They had a magic club. They had an adorable friend. They were best friends.

"Time for a snack, kids!" Mom called from the kitchen. "Come and get some fruit and crackers!"

Lily and Ben ran to the kitchen, leaving their blocks on the floor. They were hungry and wanted to eat. Mom gave them each a plate with a banana, some grapes and some cheese crackers. They sat at the table and started to munch.

"Can we watch TV after snack, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey, but only for a little while. Then you have to clean up your blocks, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom," Lily and Ben said.

They finished their snack and went to the living room. They turned on the TV and found their favorite show. It was about a silly dog and a smart cat who had adventures. They laughed and clapped at the funny things the dog did.

The dog saw a big bone in the yard. He wanted to get it, but the cat told him to be careful. There was a fence around the bone, and a sign that said "Beware of the dog". The cat said it was a trap, but the dog did not listen. He was foolish and greedy. He jumped over the fence and ran to the bone.

But as soon as he touched the bone, a loud bark came from behind a bush. It was a big, mean dog who lived there. He was angry that the silly dog tried to take his bone. He chased the silly dog around the yard, snapping and growling.

The cat watched from the fence and shook his head. He said to himself, "That dog never learns. He always gets into trouble. He should have listened to me."

Lily and Ben watched the show and felt sorry for the silly dog. They hoped he would escape from the mean dog. They also thought he was foolish and should have listened to the cat.

They were so into the show that they did not hear Mom come into the living room. She saw the blocks on the floor and frowned. She said, "Lily, Ben, I told you to clean up your blocks after snack. Why didn't you do it?"

Lily and Ben paused the show and looked at Mom. They felt guilty and ashamed. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We forgot. We were watching the show."

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We're sorry."

They turned off the TV and went to pick up their blocks. They put them in a box and carried it to their room. They said to each other, "We were foolish and lazy. We should have cleaned up our blocks. We don't want to make Mom mad. We love her."

They hugged Mom and said, "We love you, Mom. We're sorry we didn't clean up our blocks. We won't do it again."

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said, "I love you, too, kids. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, you can watch the rest of your show. But only for a little while, okay?"

"Okay, Mom," Lily and Ben said.

He thanked the cat for warning him. He said, "You were right, cat. That was a trap. I was foolish and greedy. I should have listened to you."

The cat said, "That's okay, dog. I'm glad you're safe. Maybe next time, you'll be more careful and smart."

Lily and Ben smiled and said, "Maybe next time, we'll be more careful and smart, too."

They shouted and waved at the shark boat. They hoped the people on the boat would hear them and let the fish go. But the people on the boat did not hear them. They did not see them. They did not care.

The shark boat came closer and closer. The net came closer and closer. Tim and Mia were in the way. They were scared and hurt.

"Freeze!" a voice said. It was their dad. He was on the shore. He saw what was happening. He ran to the water and grabbed them. He pulled them out of the net. He hugged them and kissed them.

"Are you okay?" he asked. "That was very dangerous. You should not go near the shark boat. They are not looking for sharks. They are looking for fish. They are not wise and friendly. They are greedy and mean."

"We are sorry, dad," Tim and Mia said. "We wanted to help the fish. We wanted to see the sharks. We did not know the shark boat was bad."

"It's okay, my loves," dad said. "I know you meant well. But you have to be careful. The sea is full of wonders and dangers. You have to respect it and protect it. And you have to listen to me and mom. We love you and we want you to be safe."

They nodded and hugged him back. They looked at the shark boat. It was going away. It was taking the fish with it. They felt sad and angry.

"Maybe one day, we will see the sharks," Tim said. "The wise and friendly ones. The ones that help the sea."

"Maybe," Mia said. "But for now, let's play on the beach. Let's make a sand castle. A big one. With a flag. A flag with a picture of a fish."

Sam was a smart boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many cars, trains, and planes that he could zoom around the floor. He also had a big sister, Lily, who liked to read books and draw pictures. Sometimes, Lily would let Sam play with her crayons and paper, but only if he was nice and asked politely.

One day, Sam saw Lily drawing a beautiful rainbow on a big sheet of paper. He wanted to draw too, but he did not want to ask Lily. He thought he was smart enough to take some crayons without her noticing. He crawled quietly to the table where Lily was working and reached for a red crayon. But Lily saw him and said, "No, Sam, those are mine! You have to ask me first!"

Sam did not like to hear no. He felt angry and wanted the crayon more. He said, "Give me the crayon! I want to draw!" He tried to grab the crayon from Lily's hand, but she held it tight. They started to pull and tug, making loud noises.

Mom heard the noises and came to see what was wrong. She saw Sam and Lily fighting over the crayon and said, "Stop that, both of you! What is going on here?"

Sam said, "Lily won't let me draw! She is mean!" He pointed at the paper with the rainbow. "I want to draw a rainbow too!"

Lily said, "Sam is trying to take my crayons! He did not ask me! He is rude!" She pointed at her hand with the red crayon. "This is my crayon!"

Mom looked at them and said, "You both need to learn to share and be kind. Lily, you have many crayons. You can let Sam use some of them if he asks nicely. Sam, you have many toys. You can let Lily play with some of them if she asks nicely. And you both can draw a rainbow together, if you want. But you have to say sorry to each other first."

Sam and Lily looked at each other and felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, Lily." "Sorry, Sam." They hugged and smiled. Mom gave them each a kiss and said, "That's better. Now, why don't you go and draw a rainbow together? I'm sure it will be very beautiful."

Sam and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom." They took some crayons and paper and went to the floor. They drew a big rainbow with many colors. They also drew a sun, a cloud, and a bird. They were happy and proud of their drawing. They showed it to Mom and said, "Look, Mom, we made a rainbow!"

Mom looked at their drawing and said, "Wow, that's wonderful! You are both very smart and creative. And you are also very good at sharing and being kind. I'm very proud of you."

Sam and Lily beamed and said, "Thank you, Mom." They gave Mom a hug and a kiss. They put their drawing on the wall and went to play with their toys. They did not fight anymore. They played nicely and had fun. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharing is better than demanding, and that kindness is better than rudeness. And they learned that drawing a rainbow is more fun with a friend.

After some time, the clever snake's home was very big. The loud bird saw this and was amazed. The bird stopped being loud and became friends with the clever snake. They played and had fun together. The clever snake was happy, and the forest was peaceful once again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to poke things with his finger. One day, Tim went for a walk and found a big icy hill. The hill was very cold and slippery. Tim wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

As he climbed the icy hill, Tim saw a toy truck. The toy truck was stuck in the snow. Tim wanted to help the truck. He started an operation to get the truck out of the snow. Tim used a stick to poke the snow around the truck. 

Tim's operation worked! The toy truck was free from the snow. Tim was very happy. He played with the truck on the icy hill all day long. When it was time to go home, Tim took the truck with him. They became the best of friends and had many more adventures together.

As Tim hopped through the forest, he heard a snap. He stopped and looked around. "Who's there?" he asked. A tiny mouse named Molly came out from behind a tree. "It's just me, Tim," she said. "I was looking for food and stepped on a stick."

Tim and Molly became good friends. They played under the quiet moon all night long. The moon watched over them and kept them safe. And they knew that no matter how dark the forest got, the moon would always be there to light their way.

Timmy learned that it's important to work hard and save up for things you want, instead of taking them without permission. And in the end, he was able to buy the big, shiny, gray apple with his own money. He was very happy and proud of himself.

In the end, the man's unusual arm caused harm to Lily and she was never seen again. Timmy was very sad and he never went back to the park again.

The mouse had to think quickly. She remembered a secret passage in the library that led to a hidden room. She ran as fast as she could and managed to escape the cat's claws. From that day on, the mouse always made sure to be careful when reading her favorite novel in the library.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly around and play with his friends. One day, Tweety was flying around the house when he saw a shiny object on the floor. He flew down to take a closer look.

The shiny object was a sharp piece of glass. Tweety didn't know that it was dangerous, so he landed on it. The glass cut Tweety's foot and he started to bleed. Tweety tried to fly away, but he couldn't because his foot hurt too much.

Tweety's friends tried to help him, but it was too late. Tweety died because of the sharp glass on the floor. His friends were sad and missed him very much. They learned to always be careful and watch out for dangerous things.

Suddenly, he saw a big tree that he wanted to cut down. He started to swing his axe, but he was too tired and weak to use it properly. The axe slipped from his hands and hit him on the head. He fell to the ground and his head was bleeding.

It looked at Lily and smiled. Lily was surprised and scared. She did not know what it was or where it came from. She asked it, "Who are you? What are you?"

She goes to the big boy and says, "Hey, stop that! You cannot take their ball. That is not fair. You have to share and be nice. If you want to play, you have to ask them first."

Tim and Sam are happy. They forgive the big boy. They say, "Yes, you can play with us. But you have to follow the rules. No shouting, no kicking, no cheating. Just have fun."

But Sara and Will do not listen. They wait until their moms are busy talking. Then they sneak away and walk to the pond. They think they are smart. They think they are brave.

They reach the pond and see some ducks. They want to feed the ducks. They find some bread on the ground. They throw the bread to the ducks. The ducks come closer. Sara and Will are happy.

But then, something bad happens. Will leans too far over the edge of the pond. He loses his balance. He falls into the water. He screams. Sara screams. The ducks fly away.

Their moms hear the screams. They run to the pond. They see Will in the water. He is scared. He is cold. He is wet. He cannot swim. He needs help.

Their moms jump into the water. They try to save Will. But it is too late. Will is gone. He is not safe. He is not happy. He is not alive.

Sara and Will are not friends anymore. Sara is sad. She is sorry. She wishes she had listened to her mom. She wishes she had not walked to the pond. She wishes Will was still here.

Lily laughs. She thinks Ben is funny. She follows him and claps her hands. "You are the best, Star Boy!"

Lily and Ben stop. They look around. They see a man coming towards them. He is big and scary. He has a beard and a leather jacket. He does not look nice.

Lily and Ben are afraid. They do not know what to do. They hold each other's hands.

"Who are you?" Ben asks. He tries to sound brave, but his voice is small.

The man is surprised. He cannot see or talk. He lets go of the helmet. He tries to get the paper off his face. He makes noises.

"Did you hear that?" Tom whispered to Lily.

"Yes, I did. What was it?" Lily whispered back.

They got out of their beds and tiptoed to the kitchen. They saw a white shape floating in the air. It had big eyes and a long mouth. It was a ghost!

The ghost saw them and said, "Boo! I am a hungry ghost. I want to eat your food."

Tom and Lily screamed and ran back to their room. They locked the door and hid under the covers.

"Go away, ghost! You can't have our food!" Tom shouted.

"Please, ghost, leave us alone! We are not food!" Lily cried.

The ghost laughed and said, "Too bad for you. I can go through walls. I will find you and eat you."

The ghost tried to rise through the door, but it could not. It bumped its head and said, "Ow! That hurts!"

Tom and Lily heard the ghost and peeked from the covers. They saw a bright light coming from the window. It was the sun.

The sun said, "Hello, children. Don't be afraid. I am here to help you. I can make the ghost go away."

The sun shone its rays on the ghost. The ghost felt hot and said, "No! I don't like the sun. It makes me melt!"

The ghost melted into a puddle of water. It was gone.

Tom and Lily cheered and said, "Thank you, sun! You saved us from the ghost!"

The sun smiled and said, "You're welcome, children. Now go back to sleep. I will watch over you."

Tom and Lily hugged each other and went back to their beds. They fell asleep, feeling safe and happy.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play and help each other. Tom has a big garden with many fruits and vegetables. Anna has a small shop where she sells cakes and pies. They are happy.

One day, a new restaurant opens near their street. The restaurant is very big and has many people. The restaurant needs fruits and vegetables for their food. The restaurant asks Tom if he can supply them with his garden produce. Tom says yes. He thinks he can make a lot of money.

Tom starts to work very hard. He picks all the fruits and vegetables from his garden and takes them to the restaurant. He does not have time to play with Anna or help her with her shop. He does not have time to water his garden or plant new seeds. He only thinks about the restaurant and the money.

Anna is sad. She misses Tom and his garden. She does not have enough fruits and vegetables for her cakes and pies. Her shop is not doing well. She tries to talk to Tom, but he is always busy. She says, "Tom, please come and play with me. Please help me with my shop. Please take care of your garden. The restaurant is not your friend. They only want your produce. They do not care about you."

Tom does not listen. He says, "Anna, you do not understand. The restaurant is great. They pay me a lot of money. They need my produce. They are my friend. You are just jealous. Go away."

Anna is hurt. She goes away. She cries.

Soon, Tom has a problem. His garden is empty. He has no more fruits and vegetables to supply to the restaurant. The restaurant is angry. They say, "Tom, you are useless. You have no more produce. We do not need you. Go away."

Tom is shocked. He says, "But, but, I worked so hard for you. I gave you all my produce. You are my friend. You said you are great."

The restaurant says, "We are not your friend. We are a business. We only care about our food. You are not great. You are foolish. Go away."

Tom is sad. He goes away. He cries.

He looks at his garden. It is dry and barren. He looks at his shop. It is empty and dusty. He looks at his street. It is lonely and quiet. He thinks of Anna. He misses her. He says, "I was wrong. I was greedy. I lost my friend. I lost my garden. I lost my shop. I lost everything."

He goes to Anna's shop. He knocks on the door. He says, "Anna, I am sorry. I was a bad friend. I was stupid. I want to play with you. I want to help you. I want to take care of my garden. Can you forgive me?"

Anna opens the door. She sees Tom. She smiles. She says, "Tom, I am glad. I was a good friend. I was patient. I want to play with you. I want to help you. I want to take care of your garden. I forgive you."

Tom and Anna hug. They are happy.

They go to Tom's garden. They water it and plant new seeds. They go to Anna's shop. They bake new cakes and pies. They go to their street. They greet their neighbors and share their food. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy. Be a good friend. Take care of what you have.

"Oh no, our arrow!" Tom says. "How will we get it back?"

"Maybe we can climb on the ladder and get it," Mia says. She runs to the garage and finds the ladder. She tries to put the ladder against the house, but it is too heavy for her.

"Stop, Mia, that is dangerous!" Tom says. "We need to ask Mom or Dad for help. They can put the ladder and get the arrow for us."

Mia does not listen to Tom. She is stubborn and wants to get the arrow by herself. She pushes the ladder harder, but it slips and falls on the ground. Mia falls with it and hurts her knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia cries. She feels sorry for being stubborn and not sharing with Tom.

Tom runs to Mia and hugs her. He says, "I'm sorry you got hurt, Mia. Are you okay?"

Mia nods and says, "I'm sorry too, Tom. I was being stubborn and not nice. Can we share the bow and arrow next time?"

Tom smiles and says, "Of course we can, Mia. You are my sister and I love you."

They go inside the house and find Mom and Dad. They tell them what happened and ask them to get the arrow from the roof. Mom and Dad put a band-aid on Mia's knee and hug them both. They say, "We are glad you are okay, and we are proud of you for saying sorry and sharing. Now, let's have some cookies and milk."

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with many trees and flowers. Sometimes they pretended they were in a forest, and they made up stories about animals and fairies.

One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had a sticker that said "send to grandma". Anna and Ben wondered what was inside. They opened the box and saw a beautiful quilt with many colors and shapes. They touched it and felt how soft and warm it was.

"Let's send it to grandma!" Anna said. "She will love it!"

"But how?" Ben asked. "We can't go to the post office. We are too little."

Anna had an idea. She ran inside and got some string and scissors. She cut a long piece of string and tied one end to the box. Then she gave the other end to Ben.

"Come on, let's go to the forest!" she said. "We can find a bird who can fly the box to grandma!"

They dragged the box to the yard and looked for a bird. They saw a robin, a sparrow, a blue jay, and a cardinal. But they were all too small to carry the box. They kept looking until they saw a big crow on a branch.

"Hey, crow!" Anna called. "Can you help us?"

The crow looked at them and cawed. He was restless and bored. He liked shiny things and puzzles.

"What do you want?" he asked.

"We want to send this box to grandma," Ben said. "She lives far away. Can you fly it to her?"

The crow flew down and pecked at the box. He saw the quilt and the sticker. He was curious and clever.

"What's in the box?" he asked.

"A quilt," Anna said. "It's very pretty and cozy. Grandma made it for us, but we want to give it back to her. She will be happy."

The crow nodded. He liked the idea of making someone happy. He also liked the challenge of flying with a box.

"OK, I'll help you," he said. "But you have to do something for me first."

"What?" Anna and Ben asked.

"You have to find me something shiny and give it to me," the crow said. "I like shiny things. They make me happy."

Anna and Ben agreed. They ran around the yard and looked for something shiny. They found a coin, a ring, a button, and a spoon. They brought them to the crow and let him choose.

The crow picked the ring. It was shiny and round. He put it on his beak and cawed.

"Thank you!" he said. "Now I'll fly the box to grandma. Where does she live?"

Anna and Ben told him the address. They wrote it on a piece of paper and stuck it on the box. They also wrote a note that said "We love you, grandma!"

The crow lifted the box with his claws and flapped his wings. He flew up in the sky and headed to grandma's house.

"Bye, crow!" Anna and Ben shouted. "Thank you!"

"Bye, kids!" the crow shouted back. "You're welcome!"

Anna and Ben watched the crow until he disappeared. They hoped he would reach grandma safely. They also hoped grandma would like the quilt and the note. They smiled and hugged each other. They were happy they had sent a gift to grandma. They were also happy they had made a new friend in the forest.

His mom explained he didn't have to try one if he didn't want to, but that they were going to stay and eat dinner. He slowly followed her inside. They both ordered dinner and it wasn't waffles.

He felt relieved but curious. He watched as other people brought their waffles out. He saw that they were smiling and some even laughed. This made him brave and eventually he asked his mom to try a waffle. 

She agreed and ordered one for him. As soon as it was brought out, he reached for a bite. It was delicious! He ate it all up and asked for another. He even asked his mom to try some.

The boy had learned that waffles weren't so scary after all. He had arrived afraid, but he left excited and full of waffles.

But no one answers. He looks at the phone and sees a picture of a palm. He does not know what a palm is. He thinks it is a big hand. He wonders why there is a big hand on the phone. He tries to touch it, but he is clumsy. He drops the phone on the floor.

The phone makes a loud noise and breaks. Sam is scared. He runs to his mom and says, "Mom, I am sorry. I broke your phone. I wanted to record my voice, but I saw a palm and I dropped it."

His mom is angry. She sees the broken phone and the palm picture. She says, "Sam, you should not touch my phone without asking. You called my boss and left a message. He heard your voice and the palm. He thinks I am not serious. He is not happy with me."

Sam feels bad. He says, "I am sorry, mom. I did not know. I just wanted to play. I love you." He hugs his mom and says, "Please, do not be mad at me."

His mom sighs. She says, "I love you too, Sam. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Phones are not toys. They are for talking and working. Next time, ask me before you use my phone. OK?"

Sam nods. He says, "OK, mom. I will ask you. I will not be clumsy. I will be good." He kisses his mom and says, "Can we play now?"

His mom smiles. She says, "Yes, we can play now. But not with the phone. Let's play with your cars and balls and books. They are more fun and safe."

Sam is happy. He says, "Yes, mom. They are more fun and safe. And I can record my voice with them. Vroom, vroom, beep, beep, honk, honk!" He laughs and runs to his toys. His mom laughs too and follows him. They play together and forget about the phone and the palm.

"But I want it. It is so cute. Please, Mommy, please," Anna begged.

Mommy shook her head. "No, Anna, you have to leave it alone. Maybe you can receive a different toy later. Come on, let's go inside."

Anna did not notice them. She went to her room. She took the caterpillar out of her pocket. She put it on her bed. She wanted to play with it. She reached for it. But the caterpillar was not alone. Lily was terrified. She did not want to taste the squash. It looked disgusting. But she did not want to lose the game. She took a small bite of the squash. It was soft and mushy.

"Yuck!" Lily spat out the squash. "It tastes disgusting!"

"Your turn," Lily said. "I dare you to eat the whole squash."

Ben was foolish. He did not care about the squash. He wanted to win the game. He opened his mouth and stuffed the squash inside. He chewed and swallowed.

"Ha!" Ben said. "I ate the whole squash. I win the game."

But then Ben felt sick. His stomach hurt. He felt like throwing up. He ran to the bathroom. He threw up the squash. It was disgusting.

Lily followed him. She saw him throw up. She felt sorry for him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I should not have dared you to eat the whole squash. It was a bad game."

Ben nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I should not have eaten the whole squash. It was a bad idea."

They hugged. They learned their lesson. They never played dare with the squash again.

"Who cares?" Tom says. "It is blue. It is cool. I want it. Give it to me."

Tom and Jen start to fight over the blue ear. They pull and tug and yell. They do not share. They do not listen. They are not nice.

Suddenly, they hear a loud roar. They look up and see a big dragon. The dragon is angry. The dragon is missing an ear. The blue ear is the dragon's ear.

"Give me back my ear!" the dragon says. "You are bad children. You took my ear. You hurt me. Now I will hurt you."

The dragon breathes fire at Tom and Jen. They scream and run away. But they are too late. The fire catches them and burns them. They are very sorry. But it is too late.

The moral of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. Do not fight with your friends. Do not ignore someone's pain. Or you might make a big mistake. And you might pay a big price.

Lily felt very proud of herself for helping her flowers. She was happy that she could be a humble gardener. From that day on, Lily took care of her flowers every day with her trusty hose.

Lily and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They wanted to give him a nose, but they did not have a carrot.

"Let's go to the garden and find a carrot," Tom said.

They ran to the garden and looked for a carrot. But the ground was icy and hard. They could not dig.

"Oh no, what can we do?" Lily asked.

Tom saw a radish on the ground. It was red and round.

"Look, a radish! We can use it for the nose," he said.

He picked up the radish and ran back to the snowman. Lily followed him.

But when they got to the snowman, they saw a bird on his head. The bird was pecking at the hat.

"Hey, bird, go away! That's our snowman!" Tom shouted.

The bird looked at Tom and Lily. It did not go away. It flew down and took the radish from Tom's hand.

"Hey, bird, give it back! That's our nose!" Lily shouted.

The bird flew away with the radish. It was hungry and liked the radish.

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They did not have a nose for their snowman.

They looked around and saw a pine cone on the ground. It was brown and pointy.

"Maybe we can use this for the nose," Lily said.

She picked up the pine cone and ran to the snowman. Tom followed her.

They stuck the pine cone on the snowman's face. It looked funny, but it was better than nothing.

They smiled and hugged their snowman.

They did not see the bird watching them from a tree. The bird did not like the pine cone. It liked the radish. It was happy and full.

Lily liked to play with her drum. She had a red drum with yellow stars on it. She liked to hit the drum with her sticks and make loud noises. She liked to make different rhythms with her drum. Sometimes she hit the drum fast, sometimes she hit the drum slow.

One day, Lily was playing with her drum in her room. She was making a regular rhythm with her drum. She hit the drum once, then she waited, then she hit the drum again. She did this over and over. She thought it sounded nice and steady.

Then, she heard a knock on the door. It was her brother, Max. Max was older than Lily. He liked to play with his guitar. He had a blue guitar with green stripes on it. He liked to strum the guitar and make soft noises. He liked to make different melodies with his guitar. Sometimes he strummed the guitar high, sometimes he strummed the guitar low.

"Hi, Lily," Max said. "Can I play with you?"

"Sure, Max," Lily said. "You can play with me and my drum."

Max came into Lily's room and sat on the floor. He brought his guitar with him. He looked at Lily's drum and smiled.

"Can I try your drum?" Max asked.

"OK, Max," Lily said. "But you have to follow my rhythm. You have to hit the drum once, then wait, then hit the drum again. Like this."

Lily showed Max how to play her drum. She hit the drum once, then she waited, then she hit the drum again. She did this over and over.

Max watched Lily and nodded. He took the sticks and tried to play the drum. He hit the drum once, then he waited, then he hit the drum again. He did this over and over. He followed Lily's rhythm.

"Good, Max," Lily said. "You are playing my drum well. Now, let's make it more fun. Let's increase the speed. Let's hit the drum faster and faster."

Lily and Max started to hit the drum faster and faster. They increased the speed of their rhythm. They hit the drum more and more times. They made louder and louder noises. They had fun playing the drum.

But then, they heard another knock on the door. It was their mom. Mom was not happy. She had a frown on her face. She did not like the noise.

"Kids, kids," Mom said. "What are you doing? You are making too much noise. You are disturbing the neighbors. You have to stop playing the drum. You have to play something quieter."

Lily and Max looked at each other. They felt sorry. They did not want to make Mom angry. They did not want to disturb the neighbors. They put down the sticks and the drum.

"Sorry, Mom," Lily said.

"Sorry, Mom," Max said.

Mom smiled and hugged them. She was not angry anymore. She was glad they said sorry.

"It's OK, kids," Mom said. "I know you like to play with the drum. But you have to play with the drum softly. You have to play with the drum gently. You have to play with the drum at a regular speed. Not too fast, not too slow. OK?"

"OK, Mom," Lily said.

"OK, Mom," Max said.

Mom gave them a kiss and left the room. Lily and Max looked at each other again. They still wanted to play with the drum. But they wanted to play with the drum nicely. They wanted to play with the drum softly. They wanted to play with the drum gently. They wanted to play with the drum at a regular speed.

So, they picked up the sticks and the drum again. They hit the drum once, then they waited, then they hit the drum again. They did this over and over. They made a regular rhythm with the drum. They made a nice and steady noise with the drum. They had fun playing the drum. And Mom and the neighbors were happy too.

One day, they were playing with the spoon in their room, when their mom called them for lunch. They left the spoon on the bed and ran to the kitchen. They ate their sandwiches and drank their juice, and then asked if they could have some cookies.

"Sure, but only one each," their mom said. "And then you have to clean your room."

Ben and Lily nodded and ran back to their room. They saw the spoon on the bed and both reached for it. They pulled and tugged, but neither wanted to let go.

"It's my turn!" Ben said.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said.

They kept pulling until the spoon snapped in half. They gasped and dropped the pieces. They looked at each other with guilty eyes.

They heard their mom coming up the stairs. They quickly hid the broken spoon under the pillow and pretended to be cleaning.

Their mom opened the door and smiled. "You're such good kids," she said. "Do you want to show me what you were playing with?"

Ben and Lily frowned and shook their heads. They hoped their mom would not find the spoon. They felt bad for breaking their favorite toy and for lying to their mom. They wished they had shared the spoon and played nicely.

Sara liked to play with her dolls in her room. She had many dolls and gave them names and stories. She liked to pretend they were her staff and she was the boss. She told them what to do and how to dress and where to sit.

One day, her mom came to her room and said, "Sara, it's time to clean up your toys. We have to go to the store soon." Sara did not want to go to the store. She wanted to play with her dolls. She said, "No, mom, I'm busy. My staff needs me. Go away."

Her mom did not like that. She said, "Sara, that's not nice. You have to listen to me. I'm your mom, not your staff. You have to clean up your toys and get ready to go. Now." She said it in a serious voice.

Her mom was very angry. She said, "Sara, open this door right now. You can't lock me out. You're in big trouble. You have to say sorry and do what I say. Or else." She said it in a louder voice. She banged on the door and tried to open it.

Sara was scared. She knew she was wrong. She did not want to make her mom angry. She did not want to be in trouble. She did not want to play with her dolls anymore. She wanted to hug her mom and say sorry. She opened the door and said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I love you. I'll clean up my toys and go to the store with you. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom was glad. She said, "Sara, I love you too. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I know you like to play with your dolls, but you have to be respectful and obedient. You can play with them later, after we come back from the store. OK?" She said it in a soft voice. She hugged Sara and kissed her.

Sara nodded. She said, "OK, mom. Thank you. You're the best mom ever. And you're the real boss." She smiled and picked up her toys. She put them in a box and put the box in the closet. She took her mom's hand and went to the store. She was happy.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, Anna saw a new toy in the shop. It was a big bear with a red heart on its chest. Anna wanted the bear very much. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no. She said they had no money for new toys.

Anna was sad and angry. She thought of a plan to get the bear. She went to Ben's house and saw that he had a lot of toys. She saw a black car that Ben liked very much. She asked Ben if she could play with the car. Ben said yes, because he was a good friend. He gave Anna the car and said, "Be careful with it. It is my favorite."

Anna took the car and ran away. She did not say thank you or goodbye. She went to the shop and gave the car to the shopkeeper. She said, "I want to trade this car for the bear with the heart." The shopkeeper looked at the car and said, "This is a very nice car. Are you sure you want to trade it?" Anna said yes, because she only wanted the bear.

The shopkeeper gave Anna the bear and took the car. Anna hugged the bear and smiled. She thought she was very clever. She went home with the bear and put it on her bed. She did not play with it. She just looked at it.

The next day, Ben came to Anna's house. He was sad and angry. He said, "Anna, where is my car? You took it and did not give it back. That was not nice. That was mean." Anna said, "I traded your car for this bear. See? It has a heart. It is better than your car." Ben said, "That was not your car to trade. It was mine. You did not ask me. You did not request. You stole it. That was wrong. You have a black heart. You are not my friend anymore." He turned around and left.

Anna felt a pain in her chest. She looked at the bear and saw that its heart was not red anymore. It was black. She realized that she had done a bad thing. She had hurt her friend and herself. She had lost the car and the bear. She had no toys and no friends. She cried and cried.

The moral of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. Do not trade what is not yours. Do not hurt your friends. Be honest and kind. Request before you take. Say thank you and goodbye. Then you will have a red heart and happy friends.

Tom was a naughty boy. He liked to make a mess and not clean up. One day, he found a big rag in the closet. He thought it would be fun to use it as a cape and march around the house. He put the rag around his neck and started to march.

"Look at me, I'm a superhero!" he shouted. He marched into the kitchen, where his mom was making lunch. He knocked over a bowl of soup and spilled it on the floor. "Oops!" he said and marched away.

He marched into the living room, where his dad was reading a book. He jumped on the couch and threw a pillow at his dad. "Pow!" he said and marched away.

He marched into his sister's room, where she was playing with her dolls. He grabbed one of her dolls and ripped off its dress. "Ha ha!" he said and marched away.

His sister started to cry. His mom and dad came running. They saw the mess Tom had made. They were very angry.

"Tom, what have you done?" his mom asked. "You have been very naughty. You have to say sorry and help us clean up."

Tom felt bad. He saw how sad his sister was. He saw how hard his mom and dad worked. He realized he was not a superhero, but a troublemaker.

"I'm sorry," he said. "I was just playing. I didn't mean to make a mess."

He took off the rag and gave it back to his mom. He hugged his sister and gave her back her doll. He helped his mom and dad clean up the kitchen, the living room and his sister's room.

He learned his lesson. He learned that playing is fun, but not when it hurts others. He learned that being a superhero means being kind and helpful, not naughty and selfish. He learned to respect his family and their things. He learned to march with love, not with rag.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. They have a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Tom is a lion and Lily is a giraffe. They roar and munch on the sofa cushions.

"Look, Tom, I have a long neck and you have a big mane!" Lily says.

"Yes, and we are very strong and brave!" Tom says.

They hear a knock on the door. They stop playing and look at each other. Who could it be?

They run to the door and open it. They see a man holding a big box. He has a hat with a flag on it. He smiles at them.

"Hello, kids, I'm from the nation of Pizza. I have a special delivery for you!" he says.

Tom and Lily are very surprised. They have never heard of the nation of Pizza. They wonder what is in the box.

"Can we see what is in the box?" Tom asks.

"Sure, but first you have to answer a question. What do you notice about my hat?" the man says.

Tom and Lily look at his hat. They see a red and white flag with a green shape in the middle.

"It has a lot of colors!" Lily says.

"That's right, but what is the green shape?" the man says.

Tom and Lily think hard. They try to remember what they learned in preschool.

"Is it a tree?" Tom guesses.

"No, it's not a tree. It's something you can eat!" the man says.

"Is it a salad?" Lily guesses.

"No, it's not a salad. It's something you can put on top of bread!" the man says.

Tom and Lily's eyes widen. They suddenly feel very hungry. They know what the green shape is.

"Is it cheese?" they say together.

"Yes, it is cheese! You are very smart, kids! You have earned your pizza!" the man says.

He opens the box and shows them a big, hot, cheesy pizza. It smells delicious.

"Wow, thank you, Mr. Pizza!" Tom and Lily say.

They take the pizza and invite the man to join them. They sit on the floor and share the pizza. They are very happy and full.

They thank the man again and wave goodbye. They go back to their toys and continue playing. They pretend to be from the nation of Pizza. They make pizza noises and eat more sofa cushions.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They had a big bowl, a wooden spoon, and some flour, sugar, and water.

"Let's stir the cake mix, Ben!" Lily said. She poured some water into the bowl and added some flour and sugar. She gave the spoon to Ben and he started to stir.

"Stir, stir, stir!" Ben said, making a funny noise. He stirred so fast that some of the mix splashed out of the bowl and onto the floor.

"Oh no, Ben! You made a mess!" Lily said. She looked around and saw some drops of mix on the table, the chairs, and the wall. She hoped Mommy wouldn't see it.

Just then, they heard Mommy's voice from upstairs. She sounded serious.

"Lily, Ben, what are you doing down there? I hear a lot of noise. Come upstairs right now!"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They knew they were in trouble. They put down the spoon and the bowl and ran upstairs.

"Sorry, Mommy, we were just playing," Lily said.

"Playing? Or making a disaster?" Mommy said. She followed them downstairs and saw the mess they had made. She was not happy.

"Lily, Ben, this is not how you play in the kitchen. You have to be careful and clean up after yourselves. You could have hurt yourselves or made a bigger mess. Look at this!" She pointed at the mix on the floor and the wall.

Lily and Ben felt bad. They knew Mommy was right. They said sorry and helped Mommy clean up the mess. They promised to be more careful next time. Mommy gave them a hug and a kiss and said she loved them. She also said they could have some real cake later, if they behaved. Lily and Ben smiled and said thank you. They learned their lesson.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to swim in the pool. They have a big pool in their backyard. They wear swimsuits and goggles. They splash and kick and laugh.

One day, they see a man in the pool. He is not their dad or their uncle. He is a stranger. He has a camera and a microphone. He smiles at them.

"Hello, kids. I am a reporter. I want to talk to you. You are famous. Do you know why?" he says.

Lily and Ben shake their heads. They do not know why. They are scared of the stranger. They swim to the edge of the pool. They look for their mom.

The stranger follows them. He says, "You are famous because you have a special steak. It is the biggest steak in the world. It is in your fridge. Can I see it? Can I take a picture of it?"

Lily and Ben remember the steak. Their dad bought it for their birthday. It is very big and juicy. They love steak. They do not want to share it with the stranger.

They say, "No, you cannot see our steak. It is ours. Go away. Leave us alone."

The stranger is angry. He says, "But I need the steak for my story. It is very important. Please, let me see it. I will give you a candy."

Lily and Ben do not like the stranger. They do not want his candy. They want their mom. They yell, "Mom, mom, help us. There is a bad man in the pool. He wants our steak."

Their mom hears them. She runs to the pool. She sees the stranger. She is very mad. She says, "Who are you? What are you doing here? Get out of my pool. Leave my kids alone."

She grabs the camera and the microphone. She throws them in the water. They splash and sink. The stranger is shocked. He says, "Hey, what are you doing? That is my equipment. That is very expensive. You have to pay for it."

Their mom says, "I don't care. You have no right to be here. You have no right to bother my kids. You have no right to want their steak. It is their birthday present. Now, get out of here. Or I will call the police."

The stranger is scared. He says, "Okay, okay, I'm sorry. I'm leaving. Please, don't call the police."

He climbs out of the pool. He runs to his car. He drives away. He is very wet and sad.

Lily and Ben hug their mom. They say, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. You saved us. You saved our steak."

Their mom says, "You're welcome, my loves. I'm proud of you. You were brave and smart. You did not trust the stranger. You did not give him your steak. You called for me. You are my heroes."

They smile and kiss their mom. They say, "We love you, mom. You are our hero."

Are you ready for your birthday dinner? I have a surprise for you. I have the biggest steak in the world. It is for you. Happy birthday, Lily and Ben."

They cheer and clap. They say, "Yay, dad. Thank you, dad. We love steak. We love you."

They sit at the table. They eat the steak. It is very big and juicy. They are very happy. They are famous. They have the best steak in the world. They have the best mom and dad in the world. They have the best birthday in the world.

His mom sees his face and smiles. She says the needle will not hurt his bear, but make him better. She says the thread will make a stitch, a little line that holds the hole together. She says the stitch will be like a kiss, a sign of love. She says his bear will be as good as new.

Tommy watches as his mom makes a stitch on his bear's tummy. He sees the hole get smaller and smaller. He sees the red thread make a line on his bear's brown fur. He sees his mom make a knot and cut the thread. He sees his mom give his bear a kiss and hand him to Tommy.

Tommy hugs his bear and feels happy. He thanks his mom and runs to his room. He puts his bear on his bed and plays with him. His bear is lively and fun, just like before. He does not mind the stitch on his tummy. He thinks it is a sign of love. He loves his bear and his mom. He is happy.

Tim and Sam were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were police and catch bad guys. They had hats and badges and toy guns. They ran around and shouted "Stop, police!" and "You're under arrest!"

One day, they saw a man in a big coat. He looked sneaky and mean. He had a bag that made a jingly sound. Tim and Sam thought he was a robber. They decided to follow him and catch him.

They hid behind trees and benches and cars. They were very quiet and careful. They saw the man go into a store. They waited outside. They saw the man come out with a different bag. It was bigger and heavier. He looked happy and scared.

Tim and Sam knew this was their chance. They ran after him and yelled "Stop, police!" The man looked back and saw them. He dropped the bag and ran away. Tim and Sam picked up the bag and opened it. It was full of shiny things. They were rings and necklaces and bracelets. They were very pretty and sparkly.

Tim and Sam were very proud. They had caught a robber and found his loot. They decided to take the bag to the real police and get a reward. They walked to the police station. They felt like heroes.

But when they got there, they saw the man in the big coat. He was talking to a lady in a uniform. She had a badge and a gun. She was a real police. She smiled and hugged the man. She said "Thank you, thank you! You found my bag! I lost it this morning. It has all my jewelry. It's very precious to me. You're very kind and brave."

Tim and Sam were confused. They looked at the man. He looked sorry and sad. He said "I'm sorry, kids. I'm not a robber. I'm a finder. I find things that people lose and try to return them. I heard the jingly sound and saw the bag. I thought it was mine. I took it and ran away. I was afraid someone would think I was a robber. I was wrong. I'm very sorry."

Tim and Sam felt silly and ashamed. They had made a mistake. They had chased a finder and took his bag. They had not caught a robber and found his loot. They had been bad and rude.

They gave the bag back to the lady. They said "We're sorry, too. We thought you were a robber. We wanted to be police. We were wrong. We're very sorry."

The lady and the man were nice and forgiving. They said "It's okay, kids. You were trying to do the right thing. You have good hearts and imaginations. You can still be police when you grow up. But you have to learn some things first. You have to be careful and respectful and honest. You have to ask questions and listen to answers. You have to know the difference between finding and stealing."

Tim and Sam nodded and agreed. They said "We will learn, we promise. We will be better police. We will be good and polite and smart."

The lady and the man smiled and thanked them. They gave them each a hug and a candy. They said "You're welcome, kids. You're very sweet and brave. You have a lot of potential. We're proud of you."

Tim and Sam felt happy and grateful. They had learned a lesson. They had made new friends. They had been forgiven and rewarded.

Lily liked to eat oranges. She liked how they were sweet and juicy and made her mouth happy. But she did not like how hard it was to peel them. She had to ask her mom or dad to help her, and sometimes they were busy or tired.

One day, she saw a big bowl of oranges on the kitchen table. She wanted one very much, but no one was around. She felt impatient. She wanted an orange now. She had an idea. She grabbed an orange and ran to the living room. She found her toy drum and put the orange on top of it. Then she took her drumsticks and started to hit the orange hard. She hoped that the orange would break open and she could eat it.

But the orange did not break. It only bounced and rolled on the drum. Lily hit it harder and harder, but it still did not break. She got angry and frustrated. She picked up the orange and threw it on the floor. Then she started to shake it with both hands, hoping to squeeze out some juice. But the orange did not give. It only felt hard and smooth in her hands.

Lily was about to cry, when she heard a voice behind her. It was her mom. She had heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily with the orange and the drum and the drumsticks. She saw the mess on the floor and the table. She was not happy.

"Lily, what are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you making such a racket? Why are you wasting a good orange?"

Lily looked at her mom with big, sad eyes. She felt sorry and ashamed. She did not mean to make a mess or waste an orange. She only wanted to eat one.

"I'm sorry, mom," she said. "I was hungry. I wanted an orange. But I could not peel it. I tried to break it with the drum and the sticks and my hands. But it did not work. It was too hard."

Mom sighed and hugged Lily. She understood how Lily felt. She remembered how she used to love oranges when she was little, too. She also remembered how hard it was to peel them.

"It's okay, Lily," she said. "I know you were hungry. But you can't break an orange like that. You need a knife or a peeler. And you need to be careful and gentle. Oranges are delicate and precious. They are gifts from nature. We should not waste them or hurt them. We should enjoy them and be thankful for them."

She took Lily and the orange to the kitchen. She washed the orange and cut it into small pieces. She put them in a bowl and gave them to Lily. She also gave her a glass of water and a napkin.

"Here you go, Lily," she said. "Now you can eat your orange. But next time, please ask me or dad to help you. We are always happy to help you. And please don't make such a noise or a mess. We have to respect our home and our things. Okay?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt better. She thanked her mom and took a bite of the orange. It was sweet and juicy and made her mouth happy. She was glad she had a mom who loved her and helped her. She decided she would not try to break an orange again. She would wait and ask for help. She would be patient and respectful. She would enjoy and be thankful for her oranges.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to see the magic marble too. She thought Ben was being lazy and mean.

"That is not fair. You have to share. We are friends. Give me the marble," she said, pulling Ben's arm.

Ben and Lily started to fight. They pulled and pushed and yelled. The magic marble slipped from Ben's hand and rolled away.

They did not see it. They were too busy fighting.

The magic marble rolled and rolled until it reached the door. It went under the door and outside.

A bird saw the magic marble. It was shiny and colorful. The bird liked shiny and colorful things. It flew down and picked up the magic marble in its beak.

It flew away with the magic marble.

Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They looked for the magic marble.

They could not find it. It was gone.

They felt sad and sorry. They had lost the magic marble because they did not share.

They hugged and said sorry to each other.

They wished they could have the magic marble back.

But it was too late.

Anna did not believe her. She did not think there were ghosts or fairies or monsters in her house. She thought mom was joking. She decided to find out who did it. She looked for clues. She saw some paw prints on the carpet. She saw some fur on the bed. She saw some teeth marks on the book.

She knew who did it. It was not a mystery. It was her dog, Spot. He liked to play with her things. He did not know how to be organized. He did not know how to put things back where they belonged. He was a naughty dog.

Anna was not happy. She told Spot to stop making a mess. She told him to be a good dog. She told him to help her clean up. She gave him a bone to chew. She hoped he would learn his lesson. She hoped he would not do it again. She loved him, but she also loved her room. She wanted it to be organized.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big sack near the bench. It was brown and dirty and had a hole in it.

"What is in the sack?" Lily asked. She was curious and brave.

"I don't know. Let's look," Tom said. He was curious and bold.

They went to the sack and opened it. Inside, they saw many things. They saw clothes and books and toys. They also saw a shiny needle. It was sharp and pointy.

"Wow, look at the needle!" Tom said. He wanted to touch it.

"Be careful, Tom. The needle can hurt you," Lily said. She was smart and careful.

But Tom did not listen. He reached for the needle. He pricked his finger. He cried out loud. It hurt a lot.

Lily hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Let me see your finger." She saw a drop of blood. She took a tissue from her pocket and wrapped it around his finger.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend," Tom said. He felt better.

They heard a voice. It was their mom. She was calling them from a distant place. She was on the other side of the park.

"Tom! Lily! It's time to go home!" she said.

They looked at each other and smiled. They put the needle back in the sack. They left the sack where they found it. They ran to their mom. They held her hand and told her about their adventure. She listened and smiled. She was happy and proud.

Lila liked to cook. She cooked with her mom and dad every day. They made soup, cake, pizza and more. Lila was happy when she cooked.

One day, Lila saw a monkey on TV. The monkey was funny and cute. It cooked bananas on a fire. Lila wanted to cook like the monkey. She asked her mom and dad if she could cook bananas. They said no. They said it was too hot and dangerous. Lila was sad.

Lila waited until her mom and dad were busy. She sneaked into the kitchen. She found some bananas and a match. She went to the backyard. She made a fire like the monkey. She put the bananas on the fire. She was excited.

But the fire was too big and harsh. It burned the bananas and the grass. It made a lot of smoke and noise. Lila was scared. She tried to put out the fire. She burned her hand. She cried.

Her mom and dad heard her cry. They ran to the backyard. They saw the fire and Lila. They were angry and worried. They called the firemen. The firemen came and put out the fire. They took Lila to the hospital. Lila had to stay in the hospital for a long time. She had a bandage on her hand. She was sorry. She learned a hard lesson. She never cooked like the monkey again.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They liked to run and play and laugh.

They saw a big red flower that smelled very good. They wanted to smell it more. But there was a bee on the flower. The bee was yellow and black and had a sharp thing on its back.

"Look, a bee!" Tom said. "Can I touch it?"

"No, Tom, don't touch the bee!" Lily said. "The bee can hurt you with its sharp thing. It can make you cry and feel bad."

But Tom did not listen to Lily. He reached out his hand to touch the bee. The bee did not like that. The bee used its sharp thing to sting Tom's hand. Tom felt a lot of pain. He screamed and cried.

"Mom, mom, help me!" Tom said. "The bee stung me! It hurts so much!"

Mom heard Tom and ran to him. She took his hand and looked at it. She saw a small red spot where the bee stung him. She kissed his hand and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. The bee stung you because it was scared. It thought you wanted to hurt it. You should not touch bees or other animals that can hurt you. You should be careful and respectful of them. They have feelings too."

Tom nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, bee. I did not want to hurt you. I just wanted to see you. You are very pretty. But I will not touch you again. I will be careful and respectful of you and other animals."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. I'm proud of you. You learned a lesson today. You should always listen to your sister and me. We love you and we want you to be safe and happy."

Tom hugged mom and said, "I love you, mom. I love you, Lily. Thank you for helping me."

Lily hugged Tom and said, "I love you, Tom. I'm glad you are okay. Let's go play some more."

They went to play some more. They had fun and they were careful and respectful of the bees and other animals. They learned that the bees have a sharp thing that can hurt, but they also have a good thing that can make honey. They learned that the red flower has a good thing that can smell, but it also has a bad thing that can attract bees. They learned that everything has good things and bad things, and they should be aware of them and act wisely. They learned a moral value.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play at the gym. The gym had many things to climb, jump, and swing on. Lily and Tom had fun every day at the gym.

One day, a new boy came to the gym. His name was Ben. Ben did not want to play with Lily and Tom. He wanted to play alone. He was not nice. He pushed Lily and Tom away from the things they liked. He said, "This is mine. Go away."

Lily and Tom were sad and angry. They tried to tell Ben to share and be nice, but he did not listen. He laughed at them and said, "You are silly. I can do what I want."

Lily and Tom had an idea. They decided to destroy the things that Ben liked. They broke the swing, the slide, and the ball. They said, "This is what you get for being mean. Now you have nothing to play with."

Ben was shocked and sad. He saw the things he liked were destroyed. He cried and said, "Why did you do this? This is not fair. You are mean."

Lily and Tom felt bad. They realized they were not nice either. They said, "We are sorry, Ben. We should not have destroyed your things. We were angry, but that was not the right way to act. We should have talked to you or told a grown-up."

Ben said, "I am sorry, too. I should not have pushed you away or laughed at you. I was lonely, but that was not the right way to make friends. We should have shared and played together."

Lily and Tom and Ben hugged and said, "We are sorry. We are friends."

But it was too late. The grown-ups who ran the gym saw the mess they made. They were very angry. They said, "You are not allowed to play here anymore. You have to go home and never come back. You have to pay for the things you destroyed. You have to learn to be nice and respectful."

Lily and Tom and Ben felt very bad. They had to go home and tell their parents what they did. They had to work hard to pay for the things they destroyed. They had to say sorry to the other kids who played at the gym. They had to find a new place to play.

The moral of the story is: Do not destroy things that are not yours. Do not be mean to others. Share and play nicely. Talk to a grown-up if you have a problem.

Lily did not like that. She complained to Mom and Dad. She said, "But I want Coco with me. He will be lonely and scared and cold." Mom and Dad said, "No, Lily, you have to listen. Coco needs his own space. He will be happy in his basket. You will see him in the morning."

Lily was sad and angry. She pouted and cried. She said, "That's not fair. That's not nice. I don't like it." Mom and Dad said, "Lily, stop complaining. You have to be a good girl and a good owner.
