Lily said good night to Coco, but she did not mean it. She went to her bed, but she did not sleep. She lay awake and thought about Coco. She wondered if he was warm and happy and safe. She missed him and wanted him with her.

She got up and tiptoed to the living room. She saw Coco in his basket. He was sleeping and snoring. He looked warm and happy and safe. Lily felt sorry for complaining. Tom laughs. He feels a tickle on his ear. He looks at the bird. He thinks it is cute and funny too. He smiles.

"Mom, what is that truck?" he asked.

"Wow, I want to be a fireman when I grow up. Can I meet a fireman, mom?" Sam said.

"Maybe, Sam. Maybe we will see one today," his mom said.

She smiled and winked at him. She had a surprise for him. She knew that today was a special day at the park. The firemen were going to visit and show their truck and equipment to the children. She wanted to introduce Sam to a fireman and make his dream come true.

They walked to the other side of the park, where a big crowd of children and parents was gathered. Sam saw the fire truck and his eyes widened. He heard the siren and his ears perked up. He smelled the smoke and his nose twitched. He felt the excitement and his heart raced.

"Look, Sam, there are the firemen. Do you want to say hello to them?" his mom asked.

"Hello, little boy. What is your name?" the fireman asked.

"I'm Sam. I want to be a fireman like you. You are incredible!" Sam said.

"Thank you, Sam. That is very nice of you to say. I'm glad you like firemen. My name is Frank. I'm happy to meet you," the fireman said.

He bent down and shook Sam's hand. He gave him a sticker that said "Junior Firefighter". He also let him touch the hose and the nozzle. He explained how they worked and what they did.

"Wow, this is so cool. Thank you, Frank. You are the best fireman ever!" Sam said.

"You are very welcome, Sam. You are a very smart and curious boy. Maybe one day you will be a fireman too. You have what it takes," Frank said.

He winked at Sam and his mom. He invited them to see the rest of the truck and the equipment. He introduced them to his other firemen friends. They all welcomed Sam and his mom and showed them around. They let Sam sit in the driver's seat, wear a helmet and a coat, and hold a fire extinguisher. Sam had the best day of his life. He learned a lot about firemen and fire trucks. He made new friends and had fun. He thanked Frank and his mom for the amazing experience. He hugged them and said goodbye.

He went home with a big smile on his face and a sticker on his chest. He told his dad and his sister everything that happened. He showed them his coloring book and his crayon. He said he wanted to be a fireman when he grew up.

"Waiting for what?" Ben asked.

Together, they created the biggest leaf pile in the park. It was so big, all the kids could jump in it. They laughed and played in the wild park all day. The animals watched and had fun, too. At the end of the day, everyone was happy and tired. The park was the best place to play.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a friendly bear named Bobo. Bobo loved to play with his friends in the forest. One day, while playing with his friends, they found a cave. They all wanted to enter the cave and see what was inside.

As they entered the cave, they saw lots of ice on the ground. Bobo and his friends were very excited to see the ice. They had never seen ice before. They slid on the ice and had lots of fun. They played on the ice all day long, laughing and enjoying their time together.

After playing on the ice, Bobo and his friends were tired but happy. They decided to go back home and tell everyone about their adventure. They all agreed to come back to the cave and play on the ice again. And from that day on, the friendly bear and his friends had a new favorite place to play.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. It was a gloomy day, but he wanted to play on the swing. He loved to swing high in the sky and feel the wind on his face. As he got on the swing, he saw a big nail sticking out of the swing's seat. Tim was scared and didn't want to sit on the nail.

He called his friend, Sue, to help him. Sue saw the nail and knew they had to fix the swing. They looked around the park and found a big rock. They took the rock and hit the nail until it was flat. Now, the swing was safe to sit on.

Tim and Sue took turns swinging on the swing. They swung high and laughed. Even on the gloomy day, they had fun at the park. They were happy they fixed the swing and could play together.

Once upon a time, there was a kind dog named Bobo. Bobo lived in a small house with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. One day, Tim's mom gave him a big box. The big box had an alarm inside. Tim was very happy.

Tim put the alarm next to his bed. That night, Bobo heard a noise. He knew the alarm would go off soon. Bobo did not like loud noises, so he thought of a plan. He went to Tim's room and saw the alarm. It was very small, so Bobo knew it would not weigh a lot.

Bobo picked up the alarm with his mouth and took it to the kitchen. He put it on the floor and waited. The alarm went off, but it was not loud. Tim and his mom came to the kitchen and saw Bobo. They laughed and thanked Bobo for being so smart. From that day on, Bobo and Tim were even better friends.

Tim went to his room and started to clean. He put his toys away and made his bed. Soon, his room was tidy. Tim showed his mom the clean room. She was happy and cooked the potato for dinner. They both enjoyed the tasty potato and Tim learned the importance of keeping his room tidy.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to look at the moon each night before he went to bed. One night, he saw something unknown in the sky next to the moon. It was big and bright, and it made him feel excited.

Tim ran to his mom and said, "Mom, look! There is something unknown next to the moon!" Tim's mom looked out the window and saw the bright thing too. She smiled and said, "That is a big star, Tim. It is called a shooting star."

Tim and his mom went outside to look at the shooting star and the moon. They sat on the grass and watched as the unknown star moved across the sky. Tim was very happy to share this special moment with his mom. After a while, they went back inside and Tim went to bed, dreaming of the moon and the shooting star.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim had a terrible whistle. Every time he tried to whistle, it sounded like a loud noise. Tim wanted to whistle just like the other birds. He felt sad.

One day, while Tim was flying in the sky, he met a wise old owl. The owl said, "Why are you sad, Tim?" Tim told the owl about his terrible whistle. The owl thought for a moment and then said, "I know! You should practice every day. Then, your whistle will become better."

Tim listened to the wise old owl. He practiced his whistle every day while he flew. Slowly, his whistle started to sound better. Tim was very happy. Now, he could whistle just like the other birds. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big field, there lived a big bull. The bull had many friends. They played together every day. The bull liked to eat a lot. He ate all the grass he could find. But sometimes, the bull ate things that were disgusting. His friends told him not to eat those things, but the bull did not listen.

One day, the bull found a big pile of disgusting food. He started to eat it all. His friends said, "Don't eat that! It's not good for you!" But the bull did not listen. He ate and ate until his tummy hurt. Then, he felt very sick.

The next day, the bull's friends came to play. But the bull was not there. He had vanished! His friends looked everywhere for him. They found him lying in his bed, feeling very sick. The bull said, "I should have listened to you. I won't eat disgusting things anymore." From that day on, the bull only ate good food, and he never vanished again. The moral of the story is to always listen to your friends when they tell you something is not good for you.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. He saw dark clouds in the sky. "Mom, will there be a storm?" he asked. His mom looked at the sky and said, "Yes, Tim, there might be a big storm soon. Be sure to come inside when it starts."

Tim went to the garden and found an enormous water gun. He thought it would be fun to spray water. He filled it up and started to spray the flowers, laughing as they got wet. He sprayed water on the trees and the grass too. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice the dark clouds getting closer.

Suddenly, the wind started to blow, and the first drops of rain began to fall. Tim remembered what his mom said about the storm. He grabbed his water gun and ran inside the house. The storm came and it rained a lot. Tim watched the rain from the window and said, "I'm glad I'm inside now."

After the storm passed, Tim went back outside with his water gun. He saw that the flowers, trees, and grass looked happy because they got more water from the storm. Tim smiled and thought, "I helped the plants too by spraying them with my water gun before the storm."

Tim played outside with his water gun every day, always remembering to come inside when a storm was coming. He knew that he could have fun and help the plants at the same time.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a shiny coin on the ground. Lily ran to pick it up, but Ben was faster. He grabbed the coin and put it in his pocket.

"Give me the coin, Ben!" Lily said. "It is not fair. I saw it first."

"No, it is mine!" Ben said. "I am faster than you. You are lazy and slow."

Lily was angry. She tried to take the coin from Ben's pocket, but he pushed her away. Lily fell on the grass and started to cry.

A big dog was walking by with his owner. He heard Lily crying and saw Ben holding the coin. He thought the coin was a toy. He ran to Ben and bit his hand. Ben dropped the coin and screamed.

"Ow, ow, ow! The dog bit me!" Ben said. "Help, help, help!"

The dog's owner came and pulled the dog away. He said sorry to Ben and gave him a band-aid. He also gave the coin to Lily.

"Here, this is for you," he said. "You can buy something nice with it. And don't fight with your friend. Sharing is caring."

Lily smiled and said thank you. She felt sorry for Ben and gave him a hug. Ben said sorry too and hugged her back.

They decided to share the coin and buy some ice cream. They ate their ice cream and played together. They were happy and forgot about the dog bite.

Sara and Ben were playing with clay. They liked to make shapes and animals with the clay. Sara made a snake and Ben made a bird. They showed each other their clay creations.

"Look at my snake!" Sara said. "It is long and green and has a forked tongue."

"Look at my bird!" Ben said. "It is red and yellow and has a big beak."

They put their clay animals on the table and went to get some water. They wanted to make the clay wet and soft.

When they came back, they saw that their clay animals were gone. Instead, there was a big mess on the table. The clay was spread all over the table and the floor. Some of it was on the walls and the curtains.

"Who did this?" Sara asked.

"It was Tom!" Ben said. "He is a bad boy. He always breaks our toys and makes trouble."

They saw Tom sitting in the corner. He had clay on his hands and his face. He also had some clay on his neck. He looked guilty and scared.

"Tom, why did you do this?" Sara asked. "You ruined our clay animals. We worked hard to make them."

"I'm sorry," Tom said. "I wanted to play with you, but you didn't let me. I was bored and angry. I didn't mean to make such a big mess."

Sara and Ben were still mad at Tom, but they also felt sorry for him. They knew he was lonely and had no friends.

"Tom, you can play with us, but you have to ask first," Sara said. "And you have to be nice and gentle with our things. You can't just break them and spread them everywhere."

"OK," Tom said. "I'm sorry. Can we be friends?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They decided to give Tom another chance. They helped him clean up the mess and make new clay animals. They had fun playing together and sharing their ideas. They learned to be kind and forgiving.

"Mom, can I have the purple ball?" Sara asked.

"Sure, honey, but you have to share with the other kids," her mom said.

Sara nodded and ran to the toy room. She picked up the purple ball and threw it in the air. She was happy.

But then, a boy came and took the ball from her. He said it was his ball. Sara was sad and angry.

"Hey, give me back my ball!" Sara said.

"No, it's mine!" the boy said.

They both pulled the ball and shouted. The other kids looked at them.

"Stop it, you two!" a lady said. She was the hotel worker. She wore a blue dress and a name tag. "This ball is for everyone to play with. You have to take turns and be nice."

Sara and the boy looked at the lady. They felt sorry.

"Sorry, lady," Sara said.

"Sorry, lady," the boy said.

The lady smiled and gave them the ball. She told them to call her Miss Anna.

"Here, you can play with the ball together. But first, you have to say sorry to each other and shake hands," Miss Anna said.

Sara and the boy did what Miss Anna said. They said sorry and shook hands. Then they played with the ball together. They had fun.

Sara and the boy became friends. They shared the ball and the other toys. They also talked and laughed. Sara was happy again.

She liked the hotel. She liked the purple ball. She liked Miss Anna. And she liked her new friend.

"Now I have a blue car and you have a yellow car. They don't match, but they are still nice." Lily says, driving her car around.

"Let's see if they can go through the tunnel together. Maybe they will be friends." Tom suggests, and they line up their cars at the entrance of the box.

"It's okay, Lily. It was an accident. I'm sorry too. Yes, please, I want my red car back." Tom says, and they hug and swap their cars again.

"Maybe we should play with something else. Something that doesn't break." Lily says, looking around.

"I have an idea. Let's play with these blocks. We can build a house or a tower or anything we want. And we can match the colors or mix them up. It doesn't matter. They are nice blocks." Tom says, pointing to a pile of wooden blocks.

"Okay, that sounds fun. Let's play with the blocks. And let's be nice to each other." Lily says, smiling.

As Toby started walking the pond grew bigger and bigger. He stopped and wondered if he had ever seen a pond so big before. He kept walking and eventually he came to a small wooden bridge that crossed the pond. But just when he stepped on the bridge he heard a loud splash in the water. 

Toby ran to the edge to see what had made that noise. A giant fat fish had jumped out of the pond and was now flopping around on land. Toby was amazed and he stayed to watch the fish go back into the pond. He had never seen a fat fish before! 

When it was time for Toby to go home he thought about the fat fish and about life. He had a whole new appreciation for the pond and he was happy to have discovered something new.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends: a puppy and an ant. The puppy was walking in the park when it spotted a broken toy car. Excitedly, the puppy picked up the car and ran to show it to the ant.

"Look what I found!" exclaimed the puppy.

The ant replied, "Nice! What are you going to do with it?"

The puppy thought for a minute and then said, "I think I'll wrap it for my friend's birthday!"

The ant spoke wisely, "Good idea! But how will wrapping it make it look better when it's broken?"

The puppy thought harder, and then said, "You're right. I shouldn't wrap it, but I should get it fixed first."

The moral of the story is that, if something is broken, it's a good idea to fix it before giving it to someone special. It helps to show how much you care!

But the pond is slippery and Sara falls in. She splashes and screams. She is scared and wet. She cannot swim. She cannot breathe. She cannot count.

Her mom hears her and runs to the pond. She jumps in and grabs Sara. She pulls her out and hugs her. She is angry and sad. She tries to calm Sara down. She gives her a massage on her back and her head. She tells her it is okay. She tells her she loves her.

But Sara does not hear her. Sara does not feel her. Sara does not see her. Sara is gone. She stopped counting.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to find twigs and make things with them. Lily made a house, and Ben made a sword. They were having fun.

But then, a big boy came and saw their twigs. He wanted to take them. He said, "Give me your twigs, or I will hit you." He was not polite. He was mean.

Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to give their twigs, but they did not want to get hit. They did not know what to do.

Then, Lily had an idea. She said, "You can have one twig, but you have to ask nicely." She gave him a twig, but it was very thin and weak. She hoped he would not notice.

The big boy took the twig and said, "Thank you." He thought he was smart. He tried to snap the twig, but it broke in his hand. He was surprised and angry. He said, "This twig is bad. It is not a good twig. I want another twig."

But Lily and Ben said, "No, you can't have another twig. You already got one. And you should be careful with twigs. They can break easily. You should be gentle and polite with them, and with other people."

The big boy felt ashamed. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry. I was rude and greedy. I should not have taken your twigs. Can we be friends?"

Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "Yes, we can be friends. But you have to be nice and share. And you have to say please and thank you."

The big boy nodded. He said, "Please, can I play with you? Thank you for forgiving me." He learned his lesson.

Lily and Ben said, "Sure, you can play with us. We have many twigs. We can make more things together." They were happy.

The moral of the story is: Be polite and respectful with others, and don't take what is not yours. You will make more friends that way. And be careful with twigs, they can break easily.

One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a crane. It had a long arm and a hook and a wheel to make it move. Ben and Mia were very excited. They wanted to try the crane.

"I'm sorry!" Mia said. She was sorry and scared. She didn't mean to break the crane. She liked the crane too.

They both looked at the crane and felt bad. They didn't want to play with it anymore. They put it back in the box and sat on the couch. They were quiet and unhappy.

Then, their mom came in. She saw the crane in the box and the sad faces on the couch. She asked them what happened. Ben and Mia told her the truth. They said they were sorry and they didn't mean to break the crane.

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay. I know you didn't mean to break the crane. It was an accident. Accidents happen sometimes. You can still play with the other toys. And maybe we can fix the crane later."

Ben and Mia felt better. They said thank you to mom and hugged her back. They felt comfortable and loved. They decided to share the other toys and play nicely. They smiled and laughed and had fun. They forgot about the broken crane. They were happy.

One day, she finds a new paper in her drawer. It is round and white, like a big circle. She thinks it is a special paper for drawing. She takes her crayons and starts to draw on it. She makes a yellow sun, a pink flower, a brown tree and a purple cat.

But when she tries to stick the paper on the wall, it does not fit. It is too big and it falls down. Lily is sad and confused. She does not understand why the paper does not fit. She looks at the paper and sees something on the back. It is a word she does not know. It says "pizza".

Lily agreed and they went to the backyard. They took turns rolling the car on the grass and watching it zoom. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot. But then, Lily had an idea. She wanted to see how fast the car could roll on the road. She thought it would be more exciting.

Lily cried and hugged Ben. She said she was sorry for taking his car and breaking it. She said she did not mean to do it and she was just curious. She said she liked his car too and she wanted to share it.

Ben and Lily looked at each other and wiped their tears. They said they were still friends and they forgave each other. They said they would find a new car to play with and be more careful. They said they learned a lesson and they would never play with cars on the road again.

Lily and Ben are friends who like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They like to race their cars on the floor and see who is faster.

One day, Lily has a new car. It is red and shiny. It has big wheels and a loud horn. Lily says, "Look at my new car! It is the best car ever! It can go very fast and make a lot of noise. Do you want to race with me?"

Ben looks at Lily's car and feels a little sad. His car is old and dull. It has small wheels and a quiet horn. He says, "Your car is very nice, Lily. But I like my car too. It is very smart and friendly. It can go very far and make a lot of music. Can we race together?"

Lily nods and smiles. She says, "OK, Ben. Let's race. But I will win, because my car is better than yours."

They set up a track on the floor and get ready to race. They count to three and push their cars. Lily's car zooms ahead and makes a loud honk. Ben's car follows behind and makes a soft tune.

But then, something happens. Lily's car runs out of oil. It slows down and stops. It makes a sad beep. Ben's car catches up and passes Lily's car. It reaches the finish line and makes a happy song.

Ben jumps and cheers. He says, "I won, I won! My car is the best car ever! It can go very far and make a lot of music. Do you want to play again?"

Lily feels a little angry. She says, "No, Ben. You cheated. You put oil in your car and I didn't. That's not fair. My car is still better than yours."

Ben feels a little sorry. He says, "I didn't cheat, Lily. I just took care of my car. Oil is good for cars. It makes them run smoothly and shine brightly. You should put oil in your car too. Then we can race again and have fun."

Lily thinks for a moment. She says, "Maybe you are right, Ben. Maybe oil is good for cars. Maybe we can race again and have fun. But I am still very competitive. I still want to win."

Ben laughs and says, "Me too, Lily. Me too. But we are also friends. And friends can play and share and help each other. Do you want to share my oil?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, Ben. Thank you. You are a good friend. And a good racer. Let's share your oil and race again. But this time, let's not be too competitive. Let's just have fun."

They hug and smile. They put oil in their cars and race again. They have fun. They are friends.

Lily liked to watch the birds in the park. She had a birdcage at home, but it was empty. She wanted to have a bird friend to sing with. One day, she saw a cute bird with yellow feathers and a red crest. It was sitting on a branch near the pond.

"Hello, bird," Lily said. "Do you want to come with me? I have a birdcage for you. You can be my friend."

The bird looked at Lily and tilted its head. It chirped softly.

"Please, bird," Lily said. "I will be nice to you. I will give you seeds and water and toys. You will be happy with me."

The bird flew down from the branch and landed on Lily's shoulder. It nibbled her ear gently.

"Yay, bird!" Lily said. "You are so sweet. Let's go home."

Lily ran to her mom, who was sitting on a bench. She showed her the bird.

"Mom, look! I found a bird. Can I keep it? Please, please, please?"

Mom smiled and touched the bird's feathers.

"It's a very cute bird, Lily. But you can't keep it. It's a wild bird. It belongs to the park. It has a family and friends here. It would be sad in a birdcage."

Lily felt a tear roll down her cheek.

"But, mom, I love it. It loves me. It came to me. It wants to be my friend."

Mom hugged Lily and wiped her tear.

"I know, honey. But you have to let it go. It's not fair to the bird. It needs to fly and be free. You can still be its friend. You can come to the park and visit it. Maybe it will remember you and sing to you."

Lily looked at the bird. It looked at her with its bright eyes. It chirped again.

"Okay, mom," Lily said. "I will let it go. But can I say goodbye to it?"

"Of course, darling. You can say goodbye to it."

Lily kissed the bird on its head and whispered, "Goodbye, bird. Thank you for being my friend. I will miss you. I hope you are happy."

She lifted the bird from her shoulder and let it fly away. It soared into the sky and joined a flock of other birds. It turned around and waved its wing at Lily.

Lily waved back and smiled. She felt sad, but also happy. She had made a new friend, even if it was for a short time. She knew the bird was happy, too. She decided to come back to the park and look for it again. Maybe it would delay its flight and stay with her for a while. Maybe it would sing to her again. Maybe it would bring her another cute bird to meet. Lily hoped so. She loved birds.

You are not brave and strong. You are small and sweet. You should not march like that, with your tail up high and your nose in the air. You should run like me, with your tongue out and your ears back."

Lily felt better knowing that her mommy used to be scared of thunder too. She snuggled up with her mommy and listened to the rain and thunder, feeling safe and warm inside.

The bird replied, "This tree used to have green shade, like all other trees in the forest. But they all changed after a storm hit this forest. You must take good care of trees otherwise bad things can happen."

Kayleigh heeded the bird's advice and promised herself to take good care of trees and plants. She knew if she wanted the forest to be as beautiful as it was before, she'd have to help change it for the better. 

The moral of the story is that no matter how little you are, you can still make a difference. Just like Kayleigh, you can help change the world for the better.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods. They had a secret path that led to a big tree with a hole. They liked to hide in the hole and pretend they were pirates or spies.

One day, they saw a small bird on the ground. It had a broken wing and could not fly. Tom and Sam felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help it. They picked it up gently and put it in a shoe box. They decided to take it to their hole and keep it as a pet.

But on the way, they met a big dog. The dog was mean and hungry. It saw the box and smelled the bird. It barked and ran towards Tom and Sam. Tom and Sam were scared and ran away. They dropped the box and the bird.

The dog reached the box and tore it open. It grabbed the bird and ate it. It was a disgusting sight. Tom and Sam heard the bird's cry and turned around. They saw the dog and the blood. They felt sad and angry. They wished they could rescue the bird, but it was too late. The dog had killed it.

They ran back to their home and told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and said she was sorry. She said they tried to do a good thing, but sometimes bad things happen. She said they should not go to the woods alone anymore. She said the dog was dangerous and could hurt them too.

Tom and Sam nodded and cried. They missed their bird and their hole. They learned a hard lesson that day. They wished they could change the past, but they could not. The end.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. But they also liked to pretend. They pretended they were brave knights and princesses, or pirates and mermaids, or astronauts and aliens.

One day, they decided to pretend they were fairy-tale heroes. Sara said, "I will be Little Red Riding Hood, and you will be the Big Bad Wolf. You have to chase me to Grandma's house, and I have to bring her a basket of food."

Tom nodded and said, "OK, but where is Grandma's house?"

Sara pointed to a big tree with a hole in it. She said, "That is Grandma's house. But be careful, there is a witch inside. She is very mean and scary. She wants to eat us."

Tom said, "A witch? How do you know?"

Sara said, "I saw her yesterday. She had a black hat, a long nose, and a big wart. She also had a broom and a cat. She looked at me and said, 'I will get you, my pretty, and your little dog too.'"

Tom said, "But you don't have a dog."

Sara said, "I know, but she said it anyway. Maybe she was confused. Come on, let's play."

Sara took a basket with some bread and cheese and ran to the tree. Tom followed her, growling and howling. Sara was a little anxious, but she also had fun. She knocked on the tree and said, "Grandma, it's me, Little Red Riding Hood. I brought you some food."

But the voice that answered was not Grandma's. It was the witch's. She said, "Come in, my dear. I have a surprise for you."

Sara was very anxious now. She did not want to go inside. She looked at Tom and whispered, "Help me, please. It's the witch."

Tom said, "Don't worry, I will save you. I will pretend I am a good wolf, and I will scare the witch away."

Tom ran to the tree and barked loudly. He said, "Witch, witch, go away. Leave Little Red Riding Hood alone. She is my friend, and I will protect her."

The witch was surprised and afraid. She did not like wolves. She said, "Oh no, a wolf. Go away, you nasty beast. Leave me and my cat alone."

She grabbed her broom and her cat and flew out of the tree. She said, "I will be back, you little brats. You will pay for this."

Sara and Tom laughed and hugged. They were happy and proud. They said, "We did it. We scared the witch away. We are fairy-tale heroes."

They ate the bread and cheese and played some more. They did not see the witch again. They had a lot of fun.

One day, a little boy and his dog were playing in the park. They saw a big bird with a long neck and big wings. The bird was in a cage. The boy and his dog felt sorry for the bird. They wanted to help the bird escape.

They looked around and saw a man with a hat and a coat. The man was holding a key. He was the bird's owner. He was not nice. He was terrible. He shouted at the bird and hit the cage. The boy and his dog did not like the man.

They waited until the man was not looking. Then they ran to the cage and opened it with the key. The bird was happy. It thanked the boy and his dog. It flew out of the cage and into the sky. It wanted to go back to its land, where it had friends and family.

The man saw the bird fly away. He was angry. He chased the boy and his dog. He wanted to catch them and put them in a cage too. The boy and his dog were scared. They ran as fast as they could.

They saw a bridge over a river. They crossed the bridge and cut the ropes. The bridge fell into the water. The man could not follow them. He was stuck on the other side. He yelled and shook his fist. The boy and his dog were safe. They smiled and hugged. They had helped the bird escape. They were happy.

Tom and Lily were very sad. They did not like time out. They did not like their room. They did not have any toys. They did not have any fun. They wished they had listened to Mom. They wished they had tidied up their toys. They wished they had not torn the bag. They wished they had been good.

Anna felt nervous. She did not like the bridge. It looked unsafe and scary. "No, Ben, it's too dangerous!" she said. "We might fall in the water!"

Ben did not listen. He ran to the bridge and stepped on it. The bridge made a loud creak. Anna screamed. She saw Ben lose his balance and grab the railing. But the railing was weak and it broke. Ben fell into the river with a splash.

Anna was very scared. She ran to the edge of the bridge and looked down. She saw Ben in the water. He was wet and cold and crying. "Help me, Anna!" he shouted.

Anna wanted to help Ben. But she did not know how. She looked around and saw a big stick on the ground. She picked it up and held it out to Ben. "Grab this, Ben!" she said.

Ben saw the stick and reached for it. He grabbed it and Anna pulled him up. She helped him get out of the water and hugged him. "Are you okay, Ben?" she asked.

Ben nodded. He was shivering and sobbing. "I'm sorry, Anna," he said. "I was silly. I should have listened to you. The bridge was bad."

Anna smiled. She was glad Ben was safe. "It's okay, Ben," she said. "We can go home and get dry and warm. And maybe we can find someone who can restore the bridge. Then it will be good and strong again."

"Come on, Sara, we have to go!" Ben says. He grabs Sara's hand and runs to the door. He remembers what his mom told him. "If there is smoke, get out and stay out. Go to the big tree and wait for me."

They run outside and see the big tree. They also see their mom and dad. They are holding a fire extinguisher and a phone. They look worried and angry.

"Mom, Dad, what happened?" Sara asks.

"There was a small fire on the stove. We put it out, but it made a lot of smoke. Are you okay?" Mom says.

"We are okay, but we are sleepy. We were bouncing on the bed," Ben says.

"Bouncing on the bed? That's not safe. You could fall and hurt yourself. And you should never play with the fire alarm. It is for emergencies only," Dad says.

"We are sorry, Mom, Dad. We did not mean to be bad. We were just having fun," Sara says.

"I know, sweetie. But you have to be careful and listen to the rules. Now, let's go inside and check the house. Then, you can have a nap. You look very sleepy," Mom says.

Sara and Ben nod and hug their parents. They are glad they are safe and loved. They learn their lesson and promise to be good. They go inside and have a nap. They dream of bouncing on the bed, but without the smoke.

The dog picked up the stick and wagged its tail. It was happy to have a new toy. It did not care if it was a weapon or not. It just wanted to play.

Tom and Sam learned a lesson. They should not fight over things. They should be kind and gentle. They should refuse to use weapons to hurt others. They should use mild words to solve problems. They should be good friends.

"Wow, Ben, you are so good at jumping!" Lily said, as she watched him fly in the air.

"It's okay, Ben, it's not your fault," Lily said, as she sniffed.

They learned that they should respect and care for other living things. They learned that they should listen to their mom. "Yes, it does!" Ben said. "It means I'm bigger and stronger and better than you!"

"No, you're not!" Lily said. "You're just mean and rude and silly!"

Tom and Lily were two sheep who lived in a big valley with many other sheep. They liked to eat grass, play with their friends and follow their shepherd. Sometimes, they heard stories about a famous mountain that was far away from their valley. The mountain was very high and had snow on top. Some sheep said that the mountain had a magic cave where a good fairy lived.

One day, Tom and Lily decided to move and see the mountain for themselves. They told their shepherd that they wanted to go on an adventure. The shepherd was sad, but he said they could go if they were careful and came back soon. He gave them a map and a bell to ring if they needed help.

Tom and Lily moved for a long time, crossing hills and rivers and forests. They saw many new things and animals, but they also faced some dangers. Once, they met a big wolf who wanted to eat them, but they ran away and hid behind a rock. Another time, they got lost in a fog and almost fell into a hole, but they heard the bell and followed the sound back to the path.

Finally, they reached the mountain and saw the snow and the cave. They were very happy and curious. They moved closer to the cave and saw a light inside. They wondered if it was the fairy. They moved inside the cave and called out, "Hello, is anyone there?"

But instead of a fairy, they saw a big dragon who was sleeping on a pile of gold and jewels. The dragon woke up and saw the sheep. He was very angry and hungry. He roared, "Who are you and what are you doing in my cave? You are not welcome here. You are my dinner!"

Tom and Lily were very scared and sorry. They wished they had never moved from their valley. They moved back to the entrance of the cave and tried to run away, but the dragon was faster and blocked their way. He opened his mouth and breathed fire at them.

But then, they heard another sound. It was the bell and the shepherd. He had followed their map and found them. He saw the dragon and threw a big stone at his head. The dragon was hurt and distracted. He turned to face the shepherd and forgot about the sheep.

Tom and Lily saw their chance and moved quickly past the dragon. They ran to the shepherd and hugged him. They thanked him for saving them and said they were sorry for leaving. They said they did not want to see the mountain or the cave anymore. They only wanted to go back to their valley and their friends.

The shepherd was glad and proud. He said he forgave them and he loved them. He said they had learned a valuable lesson. He said the mountain and the cave were not for sheep. He said the valley was their home and their happiness.

They moved together back to the valley, ringing the bell and singing a song. They never moved again.

Jen smiles too. She says, "Okay, Tom. Let's drive your car. But I'm sorry I broke your wheel. I will give it back to you later."

Tom says, "Don't be sorry, Jen. It was an accident. I'm happy to share with you. You are my friend."

From then on, Tom was a very diligent boy. He always helped his mom whenever he could and was a great help around the house.

The little boy was sad. He knew he would be in trouble. He didn't want to make Nurse Jenny mad. He ruined her birthday surprise.

But then his friends came to help him. They worked together to get him out of the trap. They were all so brave and loyal.

Finally, their hard work paid off. The loyal tiger was free! Everyone celebrated together and had lots of fun. The loyal tiger felt very grateful to have such good friends.

One day, a little girl went on a hunt. She wanted to find something special. She looked around her house, but she couldn't find anything. So she decided to go outside.

As she stepped outside, she saw a big field with lots of green plants. She knew that this was the perfect place to start her hunt. She started walking and looking around.

Soon enough, she found something! It was a big yellow corn. It was so warm in the sun! She was so happy that she had found something she was looking for.

The little girl ran back to her house. She happily showed her mom what she found. Her mom gave her a big smile and said, "Good job! You did a great job finding the warm corn. You are so clever!"

Once there was an impatient man. He wanted to rise high so he searched for a special tool. He searched for days but never found what he was looking for. 

One day he got frustrated and threw his tools across the room. But none of the tools did what he wanted. He was so impatient he decided to climb up without any tools. 

He started to climb. He was so close to the top but then he slipped. He tumbled and fell hard. The man got hurt and he could never rise again.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable rabbit who lived in a cage. He was excited to be free one day, so he worked hard every day to try to open the cage.

One day, the rabbit decided to try something new. He wiggled and squeezed and pushed with all his might, and finally, the cage opened!

The rabbit was so happy, he hopped out and started to explore the world outside of the cage. But soon enough, he heard a loud noise and felt something scary. He jumped and looked around. He saw a big animal, who was looking right at him!

The rabbit got very scared, and started to panic. He ran as fast as he could back to his cage, and quickly hopped back in. The rabbit felt safe and happy to be back in his cage, safe from the danger outside.

The rabbit was glad to be dependable and he was now sure that he would never take the risk of leaving his cage again.

Once upon a time, a little girl was walking in a dark forest. She was very frightened, so she walked quickly. Suddenly, she saw a big bear! She knew she needed help, so ran as fast as she could.

The little girl found a cottage in deep part of the forest and rushed inside. In the corner of the room, she saw a big box. She opened it, and inside was a big knife! She was so happy and grabbed the knife.

The little girl was no longer frightened. She held the knife tightly and walked back to the bear. She was brave and shouted at the bear, and it immediately ran away.

The little girl was so happy that she had found a knife. It was her special knife and she had used it to help her out of a tough spot. She knew that having a knife was very important and that it could help her when she needed it.

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Daisy. She was very brave and loved to explore.
One night, she went on an adventure. As she walked along the path, there was a big storm and the sky was filled with lightning. It was very scary and Daisy felt scared.

But then she saw something ahead. It was a warm and friendly looking house. Daisy was brave and decided to go inside.

The old man at the house welcomed Daisy warmly. He told her that she could stay in the house until the storm passed. 
He also recommended that she stay safe and not go out in the storm.

Daisy stayed and stayed safe until the storm passed. Then, when the sky was clear, she went on her way, feeling happy and safe. 
She always remembered to listen to the old man's recommendation and stay away from the scary lightning.
